biography.plain_text: Alain Colas was a French ocean-racing sailor from the Burgundian town of Clamecy who won the single-handed transatlantic race in 1972. He became the first sailor to complete a solo circumnavigation in a multihull, demonstrating its potential for long-distance sailing. He disappeared near the Azores during the inaugural Route du Rhum.

long_biography.plain_text:
Teaching French literature in Sydney brought Alain Colas into contact with offshore sailing. He joined Éric Tabarly’s crew and began turning his voyages into newspaper reports, combining writing with photographs by fellow crewman Olivier de Kersauson. Journalism helped him pay for the racing craft he acquired with savings and a bank loan.

Colas developed an unusual way to finance a larger racing project. Regional newspapers offered advertising space in exchange for exclusive reports and photographs; he sold that space to the holiday company Club Méditerranée. Working with naval architect Michel Bigoin, he also incorporated satellite navigation and hydraulic controls into a design intended for single-handed operation.
